content.value_statement: Large repositories can lose track of issue priority, scope, and release status. This skill designs label taxonomies, applies labels in bulk, and manages milestones with GitHub CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Designs standard, minimal, or comprehensive GitHub label taxonomies.
Creates, updates, deletes, and exports labels through GitHub CLI workflows.
Applies labels to many issues using filters and helper scripts.
Creates and updates milestones with due dates and descriptions.
Reports milestone progress, label usage, and label coverage.
Suggests labels from issue title and body keywords.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI access and repository permissions before changes can run.
Bulk operations can modify many labels or issues, so review plans first.
Label inference uses simple keyword rules, not deep project understanding.
Milestone and label actions target the current GitHub repository context.

use_cases.title: Set up a new repository
use_cases.description: Create a practical label system for a new project before issue volume grows.

use_cases.title: Prepare sprint tracking
use_cases.description: Create milestones, assign candidate issues, and track completion during a sprint.

use_cases.title: Clean up inconsistent labels
use_cases.description: Find duplicate labels, missing priorities, unused labels, and naming problems.

prompt_templates.title: Create a label taxonomy
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a repository with few existing labels.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a standard GitHub label taxonomy for this repository. Review existing labels first, then recommend a minimal setup before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Label untriaged issues
prompt_templates.scenario: Organize open issues that lack labels.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find open issues without labels and suggest type, priority, and scope labels. Show the plan and wait for confirmation before applying labels.

prompt_templates.title: Create a sprint milestone
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a short sprint with milestone tracking.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a milestone for the next two-week sprint. Use a clear title, due date, description, and candidate issue filters.

prompt_templates.title: Audit label operations
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup for a mature repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit our label system for inconsistent names, missing priorities, unused labels, and milestone coverage. Recommend a migration plan with dry-run steps.

output_examples.input: Set up labels for a new repository.
output: Recommended a standard taxonomy with type, priority, and scope labels.
Prepared preset application steps and asked for confirmation before changes.
Provided a short usage guide for future triage.
Summarized total, open, and closed issues for the milestone.
Grouped progress by label so blocked areas are easy to see.
Listed practical next actions for staying on schedule.
Found naming, prefix, color, and unused-label issues.
Suggested safe renames and removals with review before execution.
Outlined verification steps after the cleanup finishes.

best_practices: Start with a small taxonomy that covers type, priority, and scope.
Use dry-run or review steps before bulk label or milestone changes.
Document label meanings so contributors apply them consistently.
anti_patterns: Creating many overlapping labels that mean the same thing.
Using labels for data that belongs in assignees, milestones, or project fields.
Running bulk cleanup without reviewing the affected issues and labels.

faq.question: Does this skill change my repository automatically?
faq.answer: It can prepare GitHub CLI actions, but you should review and confirm changes before bulk operations run.

faq.question: What tools does it need?
faq.answer: It expects GitHub CLI access, repository context, and permissions for label, issue, and milestone operations.

faq.question: Can it create milestones?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create, update, close, list, and report progress for GitHub milestones.

faq.question: Can it migrate old labels?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest renames, apply new labels, remove old labels, and document the migration plan.

faq.question: How accurate is label inference?
faq.answer: The included inference is keyword based. Review suggestions before applying them to issues.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
